_note: v2 hook overrides for le camping (B30_camping). Source hooks are kept wherever the painting shows them; these replace only hooks whose painted scene differs from the source text, so the card always describes what is in the picture.

fr_lanterne_noun.hook: Like English 'lantern', said lahn-TEHRN: a glowing LANTERN hangs from a branch at the edge of the woods, and the moths line up to dance around it.
fr_lanterne_noun.why: The painting shows a glowing camp lantern hanging from a branch with dancing moths, not a camper turning on a paper lantern.

fr_allumette_noun.hook: A MATCH flares to ILLUMINATE the dark as a boy kneeling on his little blue MAT in the grass lights a candle: ILLUMI-MAT (ah-lew-MEHT).
fr_allumette_noun.why: The painting is outdoors at the campsite (boy on a little blue mat lighting a candle), not in a dark bathroom. Oct 31 2026: the British loo-mat hook became the American ILLUMI(nate) + MAT; the painting already shows both.

fr_cabane_noun.hook: Like English 'cabin', said kah-BAHN: two children sit in their own little HUT up an oak tree, their very own cabane, with a rope ladder to climb in.
fr_cabane_noun.why: The painting shows the children already inside the finished tree hut, not nailing planks.

fr_cantine_noun.hook: Like English 'canteen', said kahn-TEEN: a hungry TEEN at the campsite CANTEEN stacks a wobbly tower of bean CANS on the counter.
fr_cantine_noun.why: The painted tower of cans stands on the canteen counter rather than on a tray.

fr_randonnee_noun.hook: A family with backpacks sets off on a HIKE, humming a RONDO ("ron-do"), while their pony neighs "NAY!"
fr_randonnee_noun.why: No music notes are painted over the hikers, so the singing becomes humming; the pony is there.

fr_pli_noun.hook: A FOLD in a map: two scouts kneel over a big map with deep creases, and one begs, with a plea ("PLEE"), to fold it right.
fr_pli_noun.why: The painting shows two scouts with the creased map (the source hook has one scout).

fr_camping_noun.hook: Like English 'camping', said kahn-PING: a boy goes CAMPING, and every time he hammers a tent peg in it PINGS like a little bell.
fr_camping_noun.why: One boy hammers the ringing pegs in the painting, not a whole family.

fr_kit_noun.hook: Like English 'kit', said KEET: a camping KIT lies open on a mossy shelf of the old stump, full of tiny tools, and a curious hedgehog peeks in.
fr_kit_noun.why: The painting shows the opened kit with a hedgehog beside it; the tiny tent stands on top of the stump rather than coming out of the kit.

fr_feu_noun.hook: Sounds like 'fur', said FEUH: a sleepy bear lies on all fours beside a SMALL cozy campfire, warming his thick FUR in its glow. Le feu is a little fire you light on purpose; a whole building ablaze is un incendie.
fr_feu_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25: feu and incendie needed a visible distinction (small campfire vs barn blaze); lesson 2: the bear is now a plain animal lying by the fire (no marshmallow stick).

fr_chaleur_noun.hook: In the summer HEAT a dog lies in the SHALLOWS ("shah-LUHR") of the paddling pool, tongue out and panting, while heat shimmers wobble in the air above him.
fr_chaleur_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25 (lesson 2): no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal is the hook; repainted so the dog no longer fans himself with a leaf. Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (sha-LUR -> shah-LUHR).

fr_camp_noun.hook: Like English 'camp', said KAHN (p silent): a big bearded camper pitches his tent at CAMP and warms a CAN of beans on a little stove.
fr_camp_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25 (lesson 2): no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal is the hook; the bear cooking beans was repainted as a bearded man.

fr_campement_noun.hook: Like English 'encampment', said kahn-puh-MAHN: a tiny CAMPSITE on top of the old stump, where two little children toast acorns over a tiny fire beside their tent.
fr_campement_noun.why: Owner review 2026-10-25 (lesson 2): no anthropomorphic animals unless the animal is the hook; the squirrels toasting acorns were repainted as two tiny children (also on the parent stump in the tent field).

fr_briquet_noun.hook: A LIGHTER flicks a flame onto a brick ("bree-KEH") barbecue.
fr_briquet_noun.why: Text pass 2026-10-28: bracketed respelling matched to the card (bree-KAY -> bree-KEH).

fr_roulotte_noun.hook: A colorful painted WAGON on wheels rolls ("roo-LOT") into the yard.
fr_roulotte_noun.why: American words 2026-10-28: the meaning word in capitals changed to its American form (same painting).

fr_dresser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe pulls the rope to put up the little tent – and the tent is wearing a DRESS (dreh-SAY)!
fr_dresser_verb.why: DRESS-ay: the tent in a dress → dresser = to put up, to set up (a tent, a table). Regular -er: RED beret. Wave 1 oct29: moved from st_croissance/st_croissance into camping/tentes; hook kept (same scene repainted).

fr_charrier_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe loads one more log onto his little CHARIOT cart to HAUL them along (shah-RYAY).
fr_charrier_verb.why: CHARIOT → charrier = to cart, to haul, to carry along. Regular -er: RED beret. Wave 1 oct29: moved from st_campeur/ecureuil into camping/tentes; hook rewritten to match the new painting.
ex: Il charrie du bois dans un petit chariot.
He carts wood in a little cart.
